The Supremum Axiom

Find the smallest ceiling over a bounded set. That ceiling, missing in the rationals, completes the reals.

The supremum is the least of all upper bounds. Ceilings are many, but the lowest one is unique. Rationals sometimes lack that lowest ceiling. The reals are the world where it always exists.

For example, measure every 🧑 classmate's height. The smallest line above them all is the supremum. It touches the tallest height exactly. Everyone fits underneath.

Answer: 1∉S1 \notin S1∈/S, but 111 is the least upper bound of SSS

Since 1−1n<11 - \frac{1}{n} < 11−n1​<1 for every nnn, 111 is an upper bound; by the Archimedean property no u<1u < 1u<1 is an upper bound, so 111 is the least upper bound, i.e. sup⁡S=1\sup S = 1supS=1.
